display.title: Episode 155: The Secret Tunnel (Chanukah)
display.summary_short: A first-night Chanukah show: the menorah inside every neshamah, a guest singer's Chanukah songs in Hebrew, English and Yiddish, and how a shul menorah once saved a whole congregation.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the first night of Chanukah. Uncle Yossi explains that when we light the menorah we also light the little menorah of our own neshamah, a light of joy and trust in Hashem that stays with us all year, which is why we sit and gaze at the candles. A guest singer then leads a medley of Chanukah favorites: Maoz Tzur, I Have a Little Dreidel, the Hebrew Chanukah, Chanukah, and an old Yiddish Chanukah song for Zeidy and Bubby. After the sponsor and the Shema with a six-year-old guest, story time brings 'The Secret Tunnel': the aged shammes Reb Beryl always polishes the shul's huge brass menorah, and at last tells why. As a boy he was in shul when armed hooligans surrounded it and gave the Jews ten minutes to live; the rabbi turned an arm of the menorah, a secret door opened, and everyone escaped through a tunnel. At Mitzvah Time children learn to put away their own toys before supper, and a caller remembers last week's lesson of thanking Mommy. The show ends with the Wonderful World of Shabbos exhibition and the new Moshiach Times.
display.lesson: The Chanukah lights kindle a lasting light in our neshamah, and Hashem guards His people in the darkest times.

date.note: First night of Chanukah 5745 ('you have probably lit your menorah by now', 'tonight and the rest of the eight days'); one week after ep 154.

advisories.note: In the story, hooligans attack Jews for practicing Judaism; many lives were lost in such attacks.
Armed hooligans surround a shul and give the worshippers ten minutes to live; all escape.
